task:
BUILD SLICE S2 OF THE V3 COLONY PLANNER: TWO DATABASE-FREE API ROUTES OVER THE MERGED `cpe` CORE. BACKEND ONLY. NO DATABASE, NO WEB/SVELTE CHANGE, DO NOT TOUCH GENERATED CLIENTS.

Context: slice S1 merged in PR #927 (`apps/api/src/cpe/`: evaluate_plan, Plan/Site/Body, validate_plan/PlanInvalid/PlanIssue, catalogue.planner_facilities/prerequisites_for, rules.rule/RULEBOOK_RELEASE, explain.explain_rule). Read those files first and reuse them; do not change any cpe behaviour. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md section 5.2 (on main, or in PR #924 if not yet merged: `git fetch origin docs/v3-colony-planner-design && git show FETCH_HEAD:docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md`). This text wins if they differ.

Do NOT touch: apps/api/src/cpe/ (no behaviour change; a new tiny helper there is allowed only if unavoidable, and must keep tests/test_cpe_boundary.py passing), optimiser/, simulation/, other routers, review_main.py, sql/, apps/web/, packages/, apps/web/src/lib/api/generated, packages/api-client/src/generated (Claude regenerates the clients afterwards). Do not add dependencies.

FILES:

1. apps/api/src/routers/plan.py — `router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/plan", tags=["v3-plan"])`. Pydantic models follow routers/v3.py's style: a local base `class PlanModel(BaseModel): model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)` for responses; request models use `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (strict for types except where noted). No database dependency anywhere in this module.

   a. `GET /catalogue`, operation_id "getV3PlanCatalogue", response_model PlanCatalogueV1 { rulebook_release: str; facilities: list[PlanFacilityV1] sorted by id }. PlanFacilityV1 { id, name, category, tier: int, allowed_location: str, economy: str | None, is_port: bool, escalating_port_tier: int | None (cp_rules.escalating_port_tier), yellow_cp_cost, green_cp_cost, yellow_cp_generated, green_cp_generated: int, prerequisites: list[list[str]] (one inner list per cpe.catalogue.prerequisites_for entry, each inner list sorted), rule_ids: list[str] } where rule_ids are what evaluate_plan would cite for a non-primary site of that facility: ['RB-0003','RB-0005','RB-0006'] for an escalating port, ['RB-0002'] if any cost or generated value is non-zero, else []. Compute it with the same helper evaluate_plan uses if one is importable without changing cpe; otherwise reproduce the rule in plan.py and add a test that it matches evaluate_plan's step rule_ids for every facility. Build the response once (functools.cache) since the catalogue is static. colony_ship is already excluded by planner_facilities().

   b. `POST /evaluate`, operation_id "evaluateV3Plan", `@limiter.limit('60/minute')` from `edfinder_api.config` (signature takes `request: Request` first, like routers/watchlist.py). Request body PlanRequestV1 { system_id64: str matching ^[0-9]{1,19}$ (string so JavaScript keeps 64-bit precision, like routers/v3.py SystemId); bodies: list[PlanBodyV1] (max_length 1000, default []); sites: list[PlanSiteV1] (min_length 1, max_length 300) }. PlanBodyV1 { body_ref: str (1..64 chars); orbital_slots: int | None (0..64); surface_slots: int | None (0..64); is_landable: bool | None; is_ringed: bool | None }. PlanSiteV1 { site_id: str (1..64); facility_id: str (1..64); body_ref: str | None (1..64); slot_kind: Literal['orbital','surface']; status: Literal['planned','building','complete','demolished']; name: str | None (max 64) }. Convert system_id64 with int() and map 1:1 onto cpe Plan/Body/Site, then call evaluate_plan. Keep the cpe validate_plan as the authority: pydantic bounds only reject malformed input early.
      Response 200: PlanEvaluationV1 { rulebook_release; system_id64: str; now: PlanTotalsV1 {t2, t3}; after_plan: PlanTotalsV1; next_port_cost: PlanTotalsV1; steps: list[PlanStepV1] (every StepResult field, same names, tuples as lists); plan_checks: list[PlanCheckV1] {code, message, rule_ids}; summary: PlanSummaryV1 {OK, BLOCKED, NEEDS_INFO, COUNTED, IGNORED: int} (field names exactly those keys); explanations: dict[str, PlanRuleExplanationV1] keyed by every rule id cited in steps or plan_checks, value {id, title, status, statement, quote, page: int | None} from cpe.explain.explain_rule }.
      cpe PlanInvalid -> HTTP 422 JSONResponse body PlanInvalidV1 { error: Literal['plan_invalid']; issues: list[PlanIssueV1 {code, site_id: str | None, message}] } in validate_plan order. Declare it in the route's `responses={422: {"model": PlanInvalidV1}}` so OpenAPI documents it (FastAPI's own pydantic 422 shape remains for malformed bodies; that is fine).

2. apps/api/src/main.py — import and `app.include_router(plan_router)` next to `app.include_router(v3_router)`. Nothing else in main.py changes. (Do NOT add it to review_main.py in this slice.)

TESTS — tests/test_plan_router.py (no database; follow tests/test_archetype_system_v3.py's pattern: `app = FastAPI(); app.state.limiter = limiter; app.include_router(plan.router)`, httpx.ASGITransport + httpx.AsyncClient, sys.path insert of apps/api/src with `# noqa: E402` on following imports; pytest-asyncio is configured with asyncio_mode = "auto"):
   A. catalogue: 200; rulebook_release equals cpe RULEBOOK_RELEASE; ids sorted, unique, colony_ship absent, count equals len(planner_facilities()); coriolis_station has escalating_port_tier 2 and rule_ids RB-0003/5/6; orbital_installation_space_farm has rule_ids ['RB-0002']; industrial_facility prerequisites == [['orbital_installation_mining_outpost']]; surface_settlement_tourism_t2_l prerequisites == [['orbital_installation_satellite']]; and for EVERY facility, rule_ids equal the rule_ids evaluate_plan gives a planned non-primary site of it (build a plan: completed orbital_outpost_civilian primary on body 'A' with 64/64 slots, landable and ringed, then that facility planned on 'A' with the right slot_kind).
   B. evaluate, Raven answer key: load tests/fixtures/cpe/raven_answer_key_praea_euq_rev174.json, POST it with each fixture site mapped to PlanSiteV1's fields only (site_id, facility_id, body_ref, slot_kind, status, name; never raven_build_type), system_id64 as a string, no bodies, assert 200, now == {t2: 1, t3: -17}, after_plan == {t2: 5, t3: -16}, len(steps) == 13, summary.COUNTED == 13, system_id64 echoed as the same string, and explanations has exactly the rule ids cited by the steps, each with a non-empty quote.
   C. evaluate, a blocked Orbis: completed orbital_outpost_civilian primary + planned orbis_t3 on one body {orbital_slots 64, surface_slots 0, is_landable true, is_ringed true}: the Orbis step result BLOCKED, reasons ['INSUFFICIENT_T3'], payers == ['orbital_installation_government','orbital_installation_medical','orbital_installation_space_bar']; next_port_cost == {t2: 3, t3: 6}.
   D. evaluate, cpe-level invalid plan (first site a space farm, valid JSON): 422, error == 'plan_invalid', issues contains code PRIMARY_NOT_PORT with that site_id. Unknown facility id: 422 plan_invalid UNKNOWN_FACILITY.
   E. malformed input rejected by pydantic with 422 (FastAPI detail list): extra field on the body; system_id64 as a JSON number; system_id64 'abc'; 301 sites; 0 sites; a name of 65 characters; slot_kind 'ring'.
   F. id64 precision: system_id64 '9223372036854775807' evaluates and is echoed unchanged.
   G. OpenAPI: build the test app's openapi() and assert both operation ids exist, the /api/v1/plan/evaluate 422 response references PlanInvalidV1, and no plan route declares a database dependency (inspect route.dependant: no dependency whose call is get_pool or get_readonly_pool).
   H. rate limit is applied: the evaluate endpoint function carries slowapi's limit (e.g. by checking limiter._route_limits contains an entry for the evaluate function's qualified name, or by sending 61 requests in the test app and expecting a 429 on the 61st — pick the deterministic one and reset limiter state in a fixture so other tests are unaffected).

VALIDATION: run exactly what CI runs: `python -m ruff check apps tests scripts shared_contracts` and `python -m ruff check apps tests scripts --select B905`, both clean; `python -m compileall -q apps`; then `python -m pytest -q tests/test_plan_router.py tests/test_cpe_boundary.py tests/test_cpe_budget.py tests/test_cpe_catalogue.py tests/test_cpe_raven_answer_key.py tests/test_cpe_rulebook_copy.py` with PYTHONPATH=apps/api/src, CORS_ORIGINS=http://test and EDDN_SIMULATION_INGEST_ENABLED=false. Then run the backend unit suite exactly as CI does: PYTHONPATH=apps/api/src CORS_ORIGINS=http://test EDDN_SIMULATION_INGEST_ENABLED=false python -m pytest --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/test_deploy_main_invariants_gate.py -m "unit or not (integration or db or operator or e2e or slow)" -q, and report pass/fail counts (tests that need PostgreSQL may error without a database; list them).
